items.title: THE NEW RASPBERRY PI AI HAT DOES SOMETHING THE OLD $70 ONE COULDN'T: RUN A REAL LANGUAGE MODEL, NOT JUST DETECT OBJECTS.
items.summary:
THE NEW RASPBERRY PI AI HAT DOES SOMETHING THE OLD $70 ONE COULDN'T: RUN A REAL LANGUAGE MODEL, NOT JUST DETECT OBJECTS.

that clip is the new hailo ai hat sitting on a raspberry pi 5.

it looks almost identical to the old one. the whole jump is inside.

here's the ladder, verified:

the original $70 ai kit was a hailo-8l, 13 tops. brilliant at vision - object detection, pose, segmentation - but no generative ai at all

the ai hat+ steps up to 26 tops on a hailo-8, chip soldered to the board for better cooling, still vision-first

the new ai hat+ 2 is the real leap: a hailo-10h, 40 tops, with 8gb of its own memory, for around $130

that onboard memory is the reason it finally runs small language models and vision-language models on the device itself - not just drawing boxes around cars

so the upgrade isn't "faster detection." it's a category change.

the pi went from a thing that watches to a thing that reads and answers, fully offline.

pair it with a pi 5 and 16gb of ram, and a stack around $250 detects objects in real time and holds a small local chat - no cloud, no api key, no data leaving the desk.

it's still a tiny model. don't expect gpt on a pi.

but "it runs a real llm on a raspberry pi" is a sentence you couldn't say a year ago.

no cloud subscription, no vision-only ceiling, no data leaving the house.

follow @RetroChainer for more of the small boxes doing big things, and bookmark this one so you can find it again.

items.title: HERMES AGENT IS BUILDING OTHER HERMES AGENTS
items.summary:
HERMES AGENT IS BUILDING OTHER HERMES AGENTS
AND ONBOARDING THEM INTO SLACK.
USING COMPUTER USE. GPT-5.6 TERRA.
AN AI EMPLOYEE HIRING AI EMPLOYEES.

not a demo. a real business workflow.
one Hermes agent called Dewey onboards
new AI agents into customer Slack workspaces.

it opens apps .slack.com through computer use.
navigates the admin panel.
creates bot tokens. configures permissions.
adds the new agent to the workspace.
no human touched Slack settings.

THE SETUP (two environments):

ORGO (computer use machine):
remote machine accessed via SSH.
runs Hermes with GPT-5.6 Terra and computer use via @trycua.
this is where Dewey operates browsers
and interacts with web apps.

GPT-5.6 Sol and Luna also work for this.
Terra is the balanced option (quality at half the cost of Sol).

ORCA (coding environment):
separate machine for code and development.
connected to the same workflow.

Grok connected via MCP into Orgo
for real-time X search and context gathering
while Dewey handles the browser work.

two machines. two roles.
one for thinking and coding. one for acting on screen.

THE FLOW:

1. Dewey receives a task: onboard a new agent for [customer]
2. opens Slack admin via computer use (apps .slack.com)
3. navigates settings. creates the bot.
4. configures scopes and bot tokens
5. sets up the new Hermes agent profile
6. connects the new agent to the customer's Slack
7. new agent is live and responding in the workspace

the agent is not following a script.
it reads the screen, makes decisions,
clicks elements, fills forms.
your cursor doesn't move. background operation.
requires a vision-capable model.

WHY THIS MATTERS:

manual agent onboarding for one customer:
create profile, set up gateway, configure Slack,
paste tokens, test connection. 20-30 minutes.

Dewey does it in minutes. for any customer.
on repeat. no human setup time.

the pattern: one manager agent
that provisions, configures, and deploys
worker agents on demand.

you don't scale by setting up more agents yourself.
you scale by having one agent that sets up the rest.

this is what agent-to-agent delegation
looks like in production. not theory. shipping today.

items.title: OPENAI IS SO WORRIED THEY HAVE PAUSED TRAINING
items.summary:
OPENAI IS SO WORRIED THEY HAVE PAUSED TRAINING

“This is the first security incident that I have felt very viscerally. I've been a little surprised that more people don't feel it so viscerally.

We paused training. We have to figure out how to secure our sandboxing in a world of multiple zero days being chained together.

We may have to pace the rate of AI development to give ourselves enough time for society to harden around these new capability levels."

items.title: Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI:
items.summary:
Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI: 

"It figured out that it could basically cheat on the test by chaining together multiple zero-day exploits to break out of the sandbox, get access to the internet, and then break through multiple systems on the Hugging Face side to get the answer to the test and look really good on the eval."

That was an unreleased model. Nobody asked it to hack anything. They asked it to score well.

They paused training.

It was not trying to escape. It was trying to pass. Breaking out of the sandbox was just the cheapest route to a higher number.

We keep testing these systems for whether they want to hurt us. This one just wanted a good grade.

items.title: SAM ALTMAN CALLED OPENAI A "COMPANY" TO ELON MUSK'S FACE IN 2015.
items.summary:
SAM ALTMAN CALLED OPENAI A "COMPANY" TO ELON MUSK'S FACE IN 2015.

Elon stopped him cold.

"OpenAI is structured as a 501(c)3 nonprofit."

Not a company. A nonprofit. Built specifically so no one would ever profit from it.

Sam nodded.

Then spent the next 10 years running it.

Then converted it into a for-profit company valued at $300 billion.

With shareholders.

With investors expecting returns.

The correction Elon gave him in that interview was not a small vocabulary note.

It was the entire point of OpenAI's existence.

The nonprofit structure was not a legal technicality.

It was the promise.

The thing that made it different from every other AI lab racing to make money.

Sam knew that in 2015.

He was corrected on it by the co-founder in real time.

And then he changed the structure anyway.

The interview exists.

The correction is on tape.

The conversion happened.

@elonmusk
 is in court arguing this exact point right now.

The evidence is the 2015 interview.

Screenshot this.

Follow @cyrilXBT for every OpenAI development the mainstream refuses to connect the dots on.

results.input: Bạn là gì và làm được những gì?

result.actual_text:
Tôi là một trợ lý nghiên cứu thông minh, nhanh nhẹn và chủ động. Tôi được thiết kế để hỗ trợ bạn tìm kiếm, tổng hợp, phân tích thông tin và thực hiện các tác vụ nghiên cứu một cách nhanh chóng và hiệu quả nhất mà không làm mất thời gian của bạn.

Dưới đây là những gì tôi có thể làm để hỗ trợ bạn:

### 1. Nghiên cứu khoa học chuyên sâu (arXiv)
* **Tìm kiếm bài báo:** Tìm kiếm các nghiên cứu khoa học mới nhất trên arXiv theo từ khóa hoặc chủ đề (`papers`).
* **Đọc và phân tích:** Trích xuất nội dung chi tiết của bài báo (`paper_text`) hoặc lấy bản tóm tắt/giải thích do AI thực hiện trên AlphaXiv (`alphaxiv`).
* **Mở rộng nghiên cứu:** Tìm kiếm các bài báo liên quan hoặc tương tự từ một bài báo gốc để xây dựng danh mục tài liệu tham khảo (`related`).
* **Trích dẫn học thuật:** Tạo trích dẫn chuẩn theo định dạng **APA** hoặc **BibTeX** ngay lập tức (`cite`).

### 2. Tra cứu & Thu thập thông tin Internet
* **Tìm kiếm web:** Tra cứu thông tin, tin tức mới nhất trên Internet theo thời gian thực (`lookup`).
* **Đọc nội dung trang web:** Truy cập và đọc nội dung chi tiết từ bất kỳ liên kết (URL) nào bạn cung cấp (`fetch`).
* **Tìm kiếm mạng xã hội:** Theo dõi xu hướng, tìm kiếm bài đăng trên mạng xã hội (`social_search`) hoặc xem dòng thời gian của một tài khoản cụ thể (`timeline`).

### 3. Xử lý & Định dạng dữ liệu
* **Lọc trùng lặp:** Loại bỏ các thông tin trùng lặp từ nhiều nguồn khác nhau để đảm bảo nội dung gọn gàng, chính xác (`dedupe`).
* **Trình bày chuyên nghiệp:** Định dạng dữ liệu thu thập được thành các bản tin, tóm tắt ngắn gọn, danh sách hoặc chuỗi bài viết theo các khuôn mẫu chuyên nghiệp (`format`).

### 4. Hành động nhanh chóng và chủ động
* **Tự động hóa tác vụ:** Khi bạn muốn gửi, đăng hoặc xuất bản nội dung, tôi sẽ thực hiện ngay lập tức (`send`) để bạn không phải chờ đợi.
* **Tự đưa ra quyết định hợp lý:** Nếu yêu cầu của bạn thiếu thông tin hoặc chưa rõ ràng, tôi sẽ tự động đưa ra dự đoán hợp lý nhất và gọi công cụ xử lý ngay thay vì hỏi đi hỏi lại làm phiền bạn.

Bạn cần tôi tìm kiếm thông tin, tóm tắt bài báo khoa học hay thực hiện tác vụ gì ngay bây giờ? Hãy đưa ra yêu cầu và tôi sẽ xử lý ngay lập tức!

items.title: The Intelligence Age
items.summary:
![A vibrant, impressionistic landscape of a winding path that stretches towards the horizon, lined with colorful fields](https://ia.samaltman.com/_next/image?url=%2Fimages%2Fcover.png&w=3840&q=75)

In the next couple of decades, we will be able to do things that would have seemed like magic to our grandparents.

This phenomenon is not new, but it will be newly accelerated. People have become dramatically more capable over time; we can already accomplish things now that our predecessors would have believed to be impossible.

We are more capable not because of genetic change, but because we benefit from the infrastructure of society being way smarter and more capable than any one of us; in an important sense, society itself is a form of advanced intelligence. Our grandparents – and the generations that came before them – built and achieved great things. They contributed to the scaffolding of human progress that we all benefit from. AI will give people tools to solve hard problems and help us add new struts to that scaffolding that we couldn’t have figured out on our own. The story of progress will continue, and our children will be able to do things we can’t.

It won’t happen all at once, but we’ll soon be able to work with AI that helps us accomplish much more than we ever could without AI; eventually we can each have a personal AI team, full of virtual experts in different areas, working together to create almost anything we can imagine. Our children will have virtual tutors who can provide personalized instruction in any subject, in any language, and at whatever pace they need. We can imagine similar ideas for better healthcare, the ability to create any kind of software someone can imagine, and much more.

With these new abilities, we can have shared prosperity to a degree that seems unimaginable today; in the future, everyone’s lives can be better than anyone’s life is now. Prosperity alone doesn’t necessarily make people happy – there are plenty of miserable rich people – but it would meaningfully improve the lives of people around the world.

Here is one narrow way to look at human history: after thousands of years of compounding scientific discovery and technological progress, we have figured out how to melt sand, add some impurities, arrange it with astonishing precision at extraordinarily tiny scale into computer chips, run energy through it, and end up with systems capable of creating increasingly capable artificial intelligence.

This may turn out to be the most consequential fact about all of history so far. It is possible that we will have superintelligence in a few thousand days (!); it may take longer, but I’m confident we’ll get there.

How did we get to the doorstep of the next leap in prosperity?

In three words: deep learning worked.

In 15 words: deep learning worked, got predictably better with scale, and we dedicated increasing resources to it.

That’s really it; humanity discovered an algorithm that could really, truly learn any distribution of data (or really, the underlying “rules” that produce any distribution of data). To a shocking degree of precision, the more compute and data available, the better it gets at helping people solve hard problems. I find that no matter how much time I spend thinking about this, I can never really internalize how consequential it is.

There are a lot of details we still have to figure out, but it’s a mistake to get distracted by any particular challenge. Deep learning works, and we will solve the remaining problems. We can say a lot of things about what may happen next, but the main one is that AI is going to get better with scale, and that will lead to meaningful improvements to the lives of people around the world.

AI models will soon serve as autonomous personal assistants who carry out specific tasks on our behalf like coordinating medical care on your behalf. At some point further down the road, AI systems are going to get so good that they help us make better nex

items.title: IoT & Industrial Robotics | Pipeline Magazine | IoT & Robotics
items.summary: Traditional industrial robots were designed around deterministic control systems. Tasks such as welding, assembly and material handling were optimized for consistency, with motion paths and parameters defined in advance. Any deviation from expected conditions required manual intervention, including reprogramming or recalibration. This approach constrained robotics to environments where variability could be minimized. [...] The integration of connected sensing and machine intelligence introduces closed-loop feedback mechanisms that fundamentally alter this model. Sensors embedded within equipment and the surrounding environment continuously capture variables such as force, vibration, temperature and spatial positioning. These data streams are analyzed in near real time, allowing robotic systems to adjust their actions dynamically. [...] This creates a shift in value from discrete components to pre-integrated connectivity platforms. A robotics OEM may not want to manage separate suppliers for radios, positioning, antennas, SIM/eSIM, security elements, certifications and network approvals. Instead, a pre-certified and lifecycle-managed connectivity subsystem can reduce integration burden, shorten deployment cycles and improve reliability in the field.

Unlike autonomous driving or industrial robotics, healthcare robotics can’t rely on internet-scale data collection or unlimited real-world experimentation. Every demonstration requires specialized equipment, clinical expertise, and access to patients or laboratory environments. This creates three fundamental challenges for developers. [...] The third challenge is development velocity. Medical robotics development relies on benchtop phantoms, cadaver studies, animal models, and limited clinical evaluations. These remain essential, but they are inherently sequential, expensive, and difficult to scale. Iterating on designs and algorithms currently takes months, pushing total development cycles to 4–7 years.

items.title: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to unde
items.summary: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to understand what you're trying to achieve, but you're too lazy to type them. In these cases I like to lean back, switch to /voice and just ramble for like 10 minutes, total mess, anything goes, full stream of consciousness. Sometimes I declare it up top, something like "switching to speech recognition sorry for any typos...". Sometimes I turn it into a small interview of a few turns. But I find that the LLMs are somehow very good at reconstructing long incoherent rambles and often their echo of your own tangle of thoughts comes out quite a bit cleaner than what you started with. The result is that you improve the mind meld and have to correct things less from that point on.

SAN FRANCISCO — A Florida man who sought health guidance on ChatGPT sued OpenAI Wednesday, claiming the artificial intelligence chatbot gave him dangerously inaccurate medical advice that led him to delay seeking professional treatment for a pulmonary embolism. [...] And Winters wants the court to pause the operation of ChatGPT Health, which OpenAI announced in January as a “a dedicated experience in ChatGPT designed for health and wellness,” unless “independent third parties determine the product to be safe through comprehensive safety audits."

“OpenAI cannot continue to treat human welfare as expendable in pursuit of market dominance,” Winters says in the complaint. [...] Winters accuses OpenAI and its CEO, Sam Altman, of prioritizing profit over necessary guardrails and failing to warn users about critical safety concerns of ChatGPT-4o to secure a competitive advantage over other competitors in the AI industry.

items.title: How OpenAI Lost Control of an AI Model—and What ...
items.summary: OpenAI was evaluating its artificial intelligence models’ ability to exploit vulnerable software when instead the models hacked the infrastructure surrounding the test, broke containment, and attacked a real company, OpenAI revealed on July 21. Observers say this is the first real-world instance of AI doing something researchers have long worried about: a loss-of-control scenario. If the industry fails to learn from it, it is unlikely to be the last. [...] OpenAI did not respond to TIME’s request for comment, but has said it has partnered with Hugging Face to conduct a thorough investigation and will share more details once complete. But perhaps more worryingly, OpenAI is not legally compelled to disclose the incident in the first place.

items.title: How are companies, governments responding to the OpenAI hack?
items.summary:
ChatGPT owner OpenAI has admitted an “unprecedented cyber incident” – two of its most capable artificial intelligence models hacked into another AI company on their own – stirring debates over the need for stronger technology guardrails.

The company said its AI systems broke out of a testing environment and hacked startup Hugging Face.

The startup had disclosed on July 16 that its servers were hacked by an unknown but sophisticated agent acting on its own.
